title: Clinic appointment-booking web app (MVP)
goal: Ship a minimal appointment-booking web app for a small medical practice: patients book, reschedule and cancel appointments online; staff manage availability; reminders go out by email.
shared_context: Stack: TypeScript, Next.js (app router), PostgreSQL via Prisma, deployed on Vercel. The practice has 3 practitioners and roughly 400 appointments a month. Patient data is personal health information and must be handled under POPIA: collect the minimum, encrypt in transit and at rest, and log access to records. Existing assets: the practice's brand colours and logo, a list of 12 appointment types with durations, and the practitioners' weekly schedules as a spreadsheet.
assumptions: Email (not SMS) is sufficient for reminders in the MVP.
open_questions: Must patients create accounts, or is booking by email + one-time code acceptable?
Who may see a patient's appointment history: every practitioner, or only the one they booked with?

subsections.title: Design the data model and booking rules
subsections.description: Design the PostgreSQL schema (Prisma) for practitioners, appointment types, availability rules, exceptions (leave, public holidays), appointments and audit logs. Specify the booking rules precisely: slot generation from weekly schedules, buffer times, double-booking prevention under concurrent requests, reschedule and cancellation windows, and time-zone handling.
subsections.rationale: Concurrency-safe booking and POPIA-compliant audit design need expert judgment; errors propagate into every later step and are hard to spot by reading.

outputs.name: booking-rules
outputs.description: Precise booking and slot-generation rules with edge cases

acceptance_criteria: Schema prevents double-booking at the database level (unique constraint or exclusion constraint).
Every rule in booking-rules has at least one worked edge case.
Audit log captures who accessed which patient record and when.
subsections.integration_notes: S2, S3 and S4 build directly on the schema and the rules.

subsections.title: Implement the slot-generation and booking API
subsections.description: Implement Next.js route handlers for listing available slots, booking, rescheduling and cancelling, following booking-rules exactly. Use a transaction with row locking (or the exclusion constraint) so two patients cannot book the same slot.
subsections.rationale: Well-specified by S1, but concurrency handling and correctness matter; tests can check most of it.
acceptance_criteria: All four operations implemented with input validation.
Concurrent booking of the same slot results in exactly one success.
Cancellation and reschedule windows from booking-rules are enforced.
subsections.integration_notes: Consumed by the patient UI (S4) and covered by tests (S5).

subsections.title: Write the email reminder job
subsections.description: Write a scheduled job (Vercel cron) that emails patients a reminder 24 hours before their appointment, with reschedule and cancel links. Include plain-text and HTML templates in the practice's brand colours.
subsections.rationale: Standard cron + email templating against a known schema.
acceptance_criteria: Reminders are sent exactly once per appointment.
Links let the patient reschedule or cancel without logging in again.
subsections.integration_notes: Uses the API's reschedule/cancel endpoints from S2 via links.

subsections.title: Build the patient booking UI
subsections.description: Build the patient-facing pages: choose appointment type, pick a practitioner and slot, enter contact details, confirm; plus a manage-booking page. Accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA), mobile-first, brand colours.
subsections.rationale: Routine UI work against a defined API; size of output is the main challenge.
acceptance_criteria: A patient can complete a booking in at most four steps.
All form fields have labels and keyboard focus order is logical.
Errors from the API are shown in plain language.
subsections.integration_notes: Final user-facing deliverable; assembled in S7.

subsections.title: Write tests for the booking API
subsections.description: Write integration tests for the booking API covering slot generation, double-booking under concurrency, reschedule/cancel windows and time-zone edge cases.
subsections.rationale: Mechanical once the rules exist; correctness is checked by running the tests.
acceptance_criteria: Each booking rule has at least one test.
A concurrency test fires 20 simultaneous bookings for one slot and expects exactly one success.
subsections.integration_notes: Run in CI; failures block the integration step.

subsections.title: Convert practitioner schedules into seed data
subsections.description: Convert each practitioner's weekly schedule from the spreadsheet export into Prisma seed records (availability rules), one practitioner at a time.
subsections.rationale: Mechanical format conversion with an exact target schema.
acceptance_criteria: Seed records validate against the Prisma schema.
Every weekly slot in the spreadsheet appears exactly once.

subsections.title: Integrate, review and prepare deployment
subsections.description: Assemble the API, UI, reminder job, tests and seed data into a deployable app; check that interfaces match (types, routes, links in emails), that POPIA requirements are met end to end, and write the deployment checklist.
subsections.rationale: Cross-cutting consistency across every artifact; compliance review raises the stakes.

outputs.name: integration-report
outputs.description: Interface mismatches found and fixed, POPIA checklist results

acceptance_criteria: Every interface between artifacts is listed and confirmed consistent or fixed.
POPIA checklist covers collection, storage, access logging and retention.
Deployment checklist includes a rollback step.
